title: GROUND STATION FOCAL PLANE ASSEMBLY AND ACQUISITION SYSTEM FOR LOW-ELEVATION OPTICAL COMMUNICATION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.087) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop the ground equipment required to enable optical communication with spacecrafts at low elevation angles,including Optical Ground Station (OGS) downlink fibre coupling and Pointing, Acquisition  Tracking (PAT) sequence elements.TargetedImprovements:The target improvement for LEO-Ground optical communication links is to increase of theoperation time by a factor of two. The target improvement forGEO-Ground optical communication links is to increase the usable spatial coverage of the GEO satellite by a factor of two.Description: To date, numerous optical satellite communication links have beensuccessfully demonstrated. Most of these experiments have operated at elevationangles exceeding 25 degrees to overcome significantatmospheric propagation challenges, such as intense turbulence. However, for LEO satellites,about half of their visibility in a circular orbit occurs between 5 and 25 elevation. Therefore, overcoming challenges with low elevation optical links coulddouble operation time. For GEO satellites, the elevation angle remains constant; however, enabling low-elevation links can potentially double thesatellite's spatial coverage on Earth. Moreover, improvements in low-elevation optical links have significant impact on both classical and quantumcommunications.This activity will examine the necessary techniques and develop the required hardware to facilitatelow elevation optical communication links through theatmosphere. This will involve namely: Study the required techniques to enable low elevation links and provide trade-off analysis Design and develop the PAT  fibre-coupled receiver systems of an OGS that enables optical communication links at low elevations Integrate the optical PAT/receiver systems to an identified OGS Perform an experimental link campaign at low elevations Analysis of the obtained results and conclude on a way forward towards higher TRL of the technology developed under this contract.

title: HIGH TEMPERATURE HEAT TRANSPORT SYSTEM FOR OXYGEN PRODUCTION ISRU PILOT PLANT - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop a high temperature heat transport system for oxygen production ISRU Pilot Plant, providing temperature control for the pilot plant vacuum distillation cavity.DescriptionThe ISRU Pilot Plant mission concept comprises the down-scaled production of oxygen in support of sustainable human lunar exploration. The oxygen production process is based on molten-saltelectrolysis of lunar regolith. One of the challenges in the ISRU Plant operation is the thermalmanagement of the processes, such as regolith sintering, electrolysis, salt recovery, fluidmanagement and processing, and LOX storage. These, take place at different temperatures, goingfrom high temperatures (up to 1100degC) to cryogenics.The plant requires a solution to provide temperature control with a variable conductance to adedicated radiator for the pilot plant vacuum distillation cavity, operating alternatively at 600degC(distillation) and 900degC (salt re-melting). Furthermore, the developed system will cover other functions such as temperature homogenization of thermal cavities for regolith processing at high temperatures and temperature control of large thermal zone operating at 750degC.This activity aims at developing a breadboard (BB) of a high temperature heat transport system for oxygen production ISRU pilot plant based which is freeze tolerant and has heat transport capabilityup to 700 W with heat transport distance of 1 m. The system shall be able to operate in temperaturerange of 400-1100degC.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of existing technologiesand trade-offs of various housing materials and workingfluids.- Development of the technical specification- Detailed design of the high temperature heat transport system- Manufacture of breadboards (BB)- Testing of the Breadboards in the specified temperature range under vacuum conditions.- Correlate test results and provide a detail assessment on the future work.

title: IN-FLIGHT ELECTRO-STATIC DISCHARGE MONITOR FOR SPACECRAFT - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop non-intrusive sensors for the characterization of Electro-Static Discharge on Spacecraft (e.g. for LEO constellations) together with an on-board events detection algorithm based on advanced approaches (e.g. AI based).Description: Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) phenomena on spacecraft have been estimated to contribute to around 20% to 25% of satellites anomalies overall.Yet, in-flight characterization of spacecraft ESDs in-flight has never been undertaken in a systematic way. In addition, while mitigation strategies are known for classical s/c configurations, new technologies (e.g. flexible solar arrays) require specific characterization in terms of risk (including in-flight) in order to demonstrate their maturity. The need for ensuring European space assetsresilience in LEO combined with the trend to mass product, fly and operate low power low mass constellation satellites calls for efficient and standardized environmental effects diagnostics, among which the one proposed here. The occurrence of ESDson Spacecraft in-flight depends on specific spacecraft electrical configurations and coupling with environments. LEO constellations growing market are subject to such risk as reported in the case of present constellations with thousands of events observed in flight (GEO (telecom, earth observation), MEO (navigation, orbit raising), as well as SSO polar environments also present a risk in that respect) due toboth surface and internal charging. From there, identifying relevant probing location on spacecraft systems where to systematicallyaccommodate non-intrusive /low resources sensors (e.g. current probes and well located RF receivers) would be of high interest to primes, spacecraft designers and agencies to improve our understanding of ESD phenomena in space and its relation to anomalies. In particular, the systematic integration of such sensors on low resource low mass constellation elements should enable large scale environmental effects diagnostics and improve the constellations resilience. This activity shall carry two phases in parallel or sequentially: Phase 1 - Review the state of the art in ESD detection and monitoring on spacecraft - Propose a concept design for a non-intrusive and system embedded method to detect, locate and measure arcing waveform signals onboard satellites - Perform breadboard testing to demonstrate critical functionalities - Define a consolidated design for an ESD monitor - Define a way forward to reach a TRL of 6 Phase 2 - Assess available methodologies (including AI/ML based) and propose a concept design for an on-board events detection algorithm - Develop a breadboard model to simulate events detection and test the detection method - Consolidate the design and propose a detailed design - Establish a development roadmap.http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses
